import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.21

by F. B. Cannonito

Is there an algorithm which decides if an arbitrary finitely presented
solvable group is metabelian?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.21»

/-- An encoded finite group presentation. The first component is the number of generators;
the second is the finite list of relators, with a word represented by a list of generator indices
and signs. -/
abbrev FinitePresentation := ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool))

/-- An encoded finite presentation is valid if every index occurring in a relator is smaller than
the declared number of generators. -/
def FinitePresentation.IsValid (p : FinitePresentation) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ p.2, ∀ x ∈ w, x.1 < p.1

/-- The relator in the free group represented by a word of a valid finite presentation. -/
def FinitePresentation.relAsFreeGroup (p : FinitePresentation) (hp : p.IsValid)
    (w : List (ℕ × Bool)) (hw : w ∈ p.2) : FreeGroup (Fin p.1) :=
  FreeGroup.mk <| w.attach.map fun x =>
    (⟨x.1.1, hp w hw x.1 x.2⟩, x.1.2)

/-- The group defined by a valid encoded finite presentation. -/
abbrev FinitePresentation.PresentedGroup (p : FinitePresentation) (hp : p.IsValid) :=
  _root_.PresentedGroup
    {r | ∃ (w : List (ℕ × Bool)) (hw : w ∈ p.2), p.relAsFreeGroup hp w hw = r}

/--
Is there an algorithm which, given an arbitrary finite presentation promised to present a
solvable group, decides whether that group is metabelian?

Here metabelian means that the second term of the derived series is trivial. No correctness
condition is imposed on invalid encodings or on presentations of non-solvable groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.21» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ decideMetabelian : FinitePresentation → Bool, Computable decideMetabelian ∧
      ∀ (p : FinitePresentation) (hp : p.IsValid), IsSolvable (p.PresentedGroup hp) →
        (decideMetabelian p = true ↔ derivedSeries (p.PresentedGroup hp) 2 = ⊥) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.21»
modeling_decisions: A finite presentation is encoded by a natural number n of generators and a finite list of relator words; each letter is a natural-number generator index paired with a Boolean sign.
Syntactic validity requires every generator index in every relator to be less than n. The algorithm has no correctness obligation on invalid encodings.
A valid encoding is interpreted as Mathlib's PresentedGroup on Fin n, with precisely the encoded words as relators.
The algorithm is a total Computable function from encoded presentations to Bool, rather than a Decidable instance attached to each group.
Correctness is required only when the interpreted presented group satisfies Mathlib's IsSolvable predicate, matching the solvability promise.
Boolean output true means that derivedSeries G 2 is bottom, the standard derived-length-at-most-two characterization of a metabelian group.

namespace Kourovka.«7.21»

/-- A computable code for a finite group presentation. The first component is
its number of generators. A relator is a list of generator indices paired with
a flag recording whether that generator is inverted. -/
abbrev FinitePresentationCode := ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool))

/-- Interpret a word in the free group on `Fin n`. An index outside `Fin n` is
interpreted as the identity, making the interpretation total on presentation
codes. -/
def word (n : ℕ) : List (ℕ × Bool) → FreeGroup (Fin n)

  | (i, inverse) :: w =>
      (if h : i < n then
        if inverse then (FreeGroup.of ⟨i, h⟩)⁻¹ else FreeGroup.of ⟨i, h⟩
      else 1) * word n w

/-- The group presented by a finite presentation code. -/
abbrev presentedGroup (p : FinitePresentationCode) :=
  PresentedGroup (↑(p.2.map (word p.1)).toFinset : Set (FreeGroup (Fin p.1)))

/--
Is there an algorithm which, given an arbitrary finite presentation under the
promise that its presented group is solvable, decides whether that group is
metabelian? Here metabelian means that the second term of the derived series is
trivial. No correctness condition is imposed when the presented group is not
solvable.

      ∀ p : FinitePresentationCode,

  sorry

/-!
# Conjecture 7.21

by F. B. Cannonito

Is there an algorithm which decides if an arbitrary finitely presented solvable group is
metabelian?

A finite presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r_1, \dots, r_k \rangle$ is encoded as
the number $n$ of generators together with a finite list of relator words in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$. The question is a promise problem: an algorithm is given such a presentation,
is promised that the presented group is solvable, and must halt with the correct answer to
"is the presented group metabelian?". Nothing is required of the algorithm on presentations
of non-solvable groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.21»

/--
A finite group presentation $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r_1, \dots, r_k \rangle$: a number
`n` of generators together with a finite list of relators, each a word in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$. As in `FreeGroup.mk`, the letter `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and the letter
`(i, false)` stands for $x_i^{-1}$.
-/
structure FinitePresentation where
  /-- The number of generators. -/
  numGenerators : ℕ
  /-- The relators, as words in the generators and their inverses. -/
  relators : List (List (Fin numGenerators × Bool))

namespace FinitePresentation

/-- The group $\langle x_0, \dots, x_{n-1} \mid r_1, \dots, r_k \rangle$ presented by `P`. -/
abbrev PresentedGroup (P : FinitePresentation) : Type :=
  _root_.PresentedGroup {FreeGroup.mk w | w ∈ P.relators}

/--
A finite presentation is the same thing as a pair `(n, R)` of a natural number `n` and a list
`R` of words over `ℕ × Bool` all of whose letters are `< n`.
-/
def equivSubtype :
    FinitePresentation ≃ {q : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) // ∀ w ∈ q.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < q.1} where
  toFun P := ⟨(P.numGenerators, P.relators.map (List.map fun l => (l.1.1, l.2))), by
    intro w hw l hl
    obtain ⟨w, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hw
    obtain ⟨l, -, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hl
    exact l.1.isLt⟩
  invFun q := ⟨q.1.1, q.1.2.pmap
    (fun w hw => w.pmap (fun l hl => (⟨l.1, q.2 w hw l hl⟩, l.2)) fun _ h => h) fun _ h => h⟩
  left_inv P := by
    cases P
    simp [List.pmap_map, List.pmap_eq_map]
  right_inv q := by
    obtain ⟨⟨n, R⟩, h⟩ := q
    simp [List.map_pmap]

/-- Checking that all letters of all relators are in range is primitive recursive. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem primrecPred_forall_lt :
    PrimrecPred fun q : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) => ∀ w ∈ q.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < q.1 :=
  have h₁ : PrimrecRel fun (l : ℕ × Bool) (n : ℕ) => l.1 < n :=
    Primrec.nat_lt.comp (Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.fst) Primrec.snd
  h₁.forall_mem_list.forall_mem_list.comp Primrec.snd Primrec.fst

instance : Primcodable FinitePresentation :=
  @Primcodable.ofEquiv _ _ (Primcodable.subtype primrecPred_forall_lt) equivSubtype

end FinitePresentation

/--
A group is metabelian if its commutator subgroup is abelian, i.e. if it is solvable of derived
length at most `2`.
-/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  IsMulCommutative (commutator G)

/-- A group is metabelian iff its second derived subgroup is trivial. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_iff_derivedSeries_two_eq_bot (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsMetabelian G ↔ derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥ := by
  rw [IsMetabelian, derivedSeries_succ, derivedSeries_one,
    Subgroup.commutator_eq_bot_iff_le_centralizer, Subgroup.le_centralizer_iff_isMulCommutative]

/-- Metabelian groups are solvable. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsMetabelian.isSolvable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsMetabelian G) : IsSolvable G :=
  ⟨2, (isMetabelian_iff_derivedSeries_two_eq_bot G).mp h⟩

/-- Abelian groups are metabelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G :=
  inferInstanceAs (IsMulCommutative (commutator G))

/--
The presentation with no generators and no relators presents the trivial group, which is
metabelian.
-/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_presentedGroup_zero_nil :
    IsMetabelian (⟨0, []⟩ : FinitePresentation).PresentedGroup :=
  haveI : Subsingleton (⟨0, []⟩ : FinitePresentation).PresentedGroup :=
    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (Quotient _))
  ⟨⟨fun _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩⟩

/--
Is there an algorithm which decides if an arbitrary finitely presented solvable group is
metabelian?

That is, is there a partial computable function `f` on finite presentations such that, for
every finite presentation `P` of a solvable group, `f` halts on `P` and outputs `true` if the
group presented by `P` is metabelian and `false` otherwise? This is a promise problem: nothing is
required of `f` on presentations of non-solvable groups.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.21» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : FinitePresentation →. Bool, Partrec f ∧
      ∀ P : FinitePresentation, IsSolvable P.PresentedGroup →
        ∃ b ∈ f P, (b = true ↔ IsMetabelian P.PresentedGroup) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.21»

    PrimrecPred fun p : ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool)) =>
      ∀ w ∈ p.2, ∀ l ∈ w, l.1 < p.1 := by
  have h : PrimrecRel fun (l : ℕ × Bool) (n : ℕ) => l.1 < n :=
    Primrec.nat_lt.comp (Primrec.fst.comp Primrec.fst) Primrec.snd
  exact (PrimrecRel.forall_mem_list (PrimrecRel.forall_mem_list h)).comp
    Primrec.snd Primrec.fst

/-- Finite presentations are encoded as pairs `(n, relators)` satisfying the well-formedness
condition, so that they can serve as inputs of algorithms. -/
instance : Primcodable FinitePresentation :=
  @Primcodable.ofEquiv _ _ (Primcodable.subtype primrecPred_wellFormed)
    { toFun := fun P => ⟨(P.numGenerators, P.relators), P.index_lt⟩
      invFun := fun p => ⟨p.1.1, p.1.2, p.2⟩
      left_inv := fun _ => rfl
      right_inv := fun _ => rfl }

/-- The relators of a finite presentation `P`, as elements of the free group on
`Fin P.numGenerators`. -/
def rels (P : FinitePresentation) : Set (FreeGroup (Fin P.numGenerators)) :=
  {r | ∃ (w : List (ℕ × Bool)) (hw : w ∈ P.relators),
    r = FreeGroup.mk (w.pmap (fun l h => (⟨l.1, h⟩, l.2)) (P.index_lt w hw))}

end FinitePresentation

/-- A group is metabelian if it has derived length at most $2$, i.e. its second derived
subgroup $G'' = [G', G']$ is trivial; equivalently, its commutator subgroup $G'$ is abelian. -/
def IsMetabelian (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  derivedSeries G 2 = ⊥

/-- A group is metabelian if and only if its commutator subgroup is abelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isMetabelian_iff_isMulCommutative_commutator (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    IsMetabelian G ↔ IsMulCommutative (commutator G) := by
  rw [IsMetabelian, derivedSeries_succ, derivedSeries_one,
    Subgroup.commutator_eq_bot_iff_le_centralizer, Subgroup.le_centralizer_iff_isMulCommutative]

/-- Every metabelian group is solvable. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsMetabelian.isSolvable {G : Type*} [Group G] (h : IsMetabelian G) : IsSolvable G :=
  ⟨⟨2, h⟩⟩

/-- Every abelian group is metabelian. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsMetabelian.of_commGroup (G : Type*) [CommGroup G] : IsMetabelian G := by
  rw [isMetabelian_iff_isMulCommutative_commutator]
  infer_instance

/-!
# Conjecture 7.21

by F. B. Cannonito

Is there an algorithm which decides if an arbitrary finitely presented solvable group is
metabelian?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.21»

/-- A finite group-presentation code. The first component is the number of generators, and the
second is the finite list of relators, each represented as a word of signed generator indices. -/
abbrev FinitePresentation := ℕ × List (List (ℕ × Bool))

namespace FinitePresentation

/-- A presentation code is valid when every generator index occurring in a relator is smaller
than the declared number of generators. -/
def IsValid (P : FinitePresentation) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ P.2, ∀ x ∈ w, x.1 < P.1

private def relator (n : ℕ) (w : List (ℕ × Bool)) : FreeGroup (Fin n) :=
  FreeGroup.mk <| w.filterMap fun x ↦ if h : x.1 < n then some (⟨x.1, h⟩, x.2) else none

/-- The group presented by a finite presentation code. On valid codes, this is the quotient of the
free group on the declared generators by the normal closure of the declared relators. -/
def Group (P : FinitePresentation) : Type :=
  PresentedGroup {r | r ∈ P.2.map (relator P.1)}

instance (P : FinitePresentation) : _root_.Group P.Group := PresentedGroup.instGroup _

end FinitePresentation

/--
Is there an algorithm which decides whether an arbitrary finitely presented solvable group is
metabelian?

Here `f` is one uniform computable algorithm on finite presentation codes. Correctness is required
only for valid presentations whose presented groups are solvable. A group is metabelian precisely
when the second term of its derived series is trivial.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.21» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ f : FinitePresentation → Bool, Computable f ∧
      ∀ P : FinitePresentation, P.IsValid → IsSolvable P.Group →
        (f P = true ↔ derivedSeries P.Group 2 = ⊥) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.21»
